Prevention: Remove and burn infected crop residue of the previous season
Timely harvest of cobs at physiological maturity to avoid infestations starting from the field
Ensure that only undamaged cobs are selected immediately after harvest, shelled and grains dried properly
Inspect grains during drying to ensure that they are properly dried and sieve maize grain to remove debris before storage
Use clean storage facilities, ensure cracks, crevices and holes are sealed
Keep grains in a well- ventillated store
Treat grain before storage in areas with high incidence (see direct controls)
Monitoring: Monitor cobs at maturity to ensure early harvesting in order to reduce field infestation
Sample grains in storage regularly at 2 weeks intervals.
Look for adults and powder from damaged grain to detect early infestation.
The body of the adult is usually black/dark brown and 3-4.5 mm long with 2 segmented antennae.
Pheromone traps or sticky traps to detect the presence of adults for early decision making
Control as soon as signs of infestation are observed (e.g. maize turning into powder) or the presence of
LGB damage (3%) in cobs is observed.
